text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Kuwait's Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah to be discharged from hospital Monday. Sheikh Saad flew to London earlier this month for follow-up treatment after colon surgery in Kuwait.
- Information Minister Sheikh Saud Nasser al-Sabah wants ministry budget boost. He said wages amount to 40 million dinars ($132 million) of the 59 million budget.
- Communications, Electricity and Water Minister Jassem al-Oun says contracts of foreign state workers will not be extended after they become 60-years-old.

- Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi says 470 Kuwaitis working in local marketing activities at the Kuwait National Petroleum Company (KNPC) will be gradually transferred to other departments after cabinet's decision to privatise local marketing of oil products was approved.
- Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), the state investment arm, plans to sell shares worth 26 million dinars in 12 listed companies.
- British Exports to Kuwait rose to 600 million pounds in 1996 from 295 million in the previous year, visiting British businessmen say.
- Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah to head the first meeting of the National Security Council.
- Kuwait expresses concern and dissatisfaction over Israel's construction of a settlement in East Jerusalem.
